title: TB Drug Resistance: Xpert MTB/RIF, the 1% Rule and M. bovis
summary: Learn what Xpert MTB/RIF detects and how accurate it is, how the agar proportion method calls resistance with the 1% rule, why every initial isolate is tested against the four RIPE drugs, and why M. bovis is intrinsically pyrazinamide resistant.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 59 Hit 6 (Xpert MTB/RIF: MTBC plus rifampin resistance via rpoB, accuracy, < 2 h), Hit 7 (agar proportion 1% rule), Hit 8 (RIPE; test initial isolates to all four drugs) and Trap 5 (M. bovis intrinsically pyrazinamide resistant). Checked against Horne 2019 (Cochrane), Boehme 2010 (read via a page-fetch tool), Lewinsohn 2017 and Nahid 2016 (ATS/IDSA/CDC guidelines; read via a page-fetch tool, Nahid only partly), Yusoof 2022, Said 2012, Fang 2025 and Singh 2022. The reviewer’s Xpert figures (specificity 100%, smear-negative 69–72%) are replaced with Cochrane pooled figures (98%; 67%, 62–72%) — register flag rv-xpert-pooled-accuracy. Pending: the 81-bp fragment as the assay target, hands-on time < 5 min, the 28-day susceptibility turnaround target, M. bovis niacin/nitrate reactions. RIPE and the four-drug panel are US (ATS/CDC/IDSA) recommendations; Philippine programme rules are not covered (register flag rv-tb-dst-us-guideline).

objectives: Describe what Xpert MTB/RIF detects, its pooled accuracy, and why a negative result in smear-negative sputum cannot exclude tuberculosis.
Interpret an agar proportion result using the 1% rule.
Name the RIPE drugs tested on initial isolates and explain why a pyrazinamide-only resistant MTBC isolate suggests M. bovis.

scenes.title: Three TB results, three decisions
scenes.altText: Invented scenario: three tuberculosis results land on one bench. (1) Sputum from a previously treated patient: Xpert MTB/RIF “MTB detected · rifampicin resistance detected”, under 2 hours. (2) An agar proportion plate: colonies on the isoniazid quadrant equal 3% of the drug-free control count. (3) A Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex isolate resistant only to pyrazinamide, from a patient who drinks unpasteurised milk. Question token: “What does each result mean?”

cues.text: Three tuberculosis results arrive. First, a molecular cartridge test on sputum from a previously treated patient: tuberculosis complex detected, rifampicin resistance detected.
Second, a susceptibility plate: colonies on the isoniazid quadrant come to three percent of the drug-free control.
Third, a complex isolate resistant only to pyrazinamide, from a patient who drinks unpasteurised milk. What does each result mean?

scenes.title: What Xpert MTB/RIF sees
scenes.altText: Schematic of the rpoB gene with a short highlighted resistance-determining region and five coloured probe marks. Cards: “Target” — PCR of an MTB-specific rpoB sequence; molecular beacons recognise the wild-type (susceptible) sequence of the region where most rifampicin-resistance mutations lie. “Speed and scope” — MTB complex plus rifampicin resistance within 2 hours, minimal hands-on time; cannot tell M. bovis from M. tuberculosis. “TB detection (Cochrane 2019)” — pooled sensitivity 98% smear-positive, 67% smear-negative culture-positive; specificity 98%. “Rifampicin resistance” — pooled sensitivity 96%, specificity 98%.

cues.text: Xpert MTB/RIF is a cartridge PCR. It amplifies a tuberculosis-specific stretch of the rpoB gene, and molecular beacons check the short region where most rifampicin-resistance mutations sit.

It reports tuberculosis complex and rifampicin resistance within two hours, with little hands-on time. Because it detects the whole complex, it cannot tell Mycobacterium bovis from Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

In the 2019 Cochrane review, pooled sensitivity was ninety-eight percent in smear-positive and sixty-seven percent in smear-negative, culture-positive adults, with specificity of ninety-eight percent.
For rifampicin resistance, pooled sensitivity was ninety-six percent and specificity ninety-eight percent. In a smear-negative patient, a negative result cannot exclude pulmonary tuberculosis.

scenes.title: Growth-based testing: the 1% rule
scenes.altText: Schematic six-well Middlebrook 7H11 agar plate: two drug-free wells (one proportional control inoculated with a 1:100 dilution, one quality control) and four wells containing drugs at CLSI critical concentrations, each inoculated with 0.1 mL of the undiluted suspension. Rule card: resistant when colonies on a drug-containing quadrant are more than 1% of colonies on the drug-free control. Time card: plates read at 7, 10, 14 and 21 days in one protocol; agar DST about 21–28 days in one review’s table; overall 28–42 days or longer when the isolate must first be grown. Order card: rapid molecular rifampicin test for at-risk patients (ATS/IDSA/CDC 2017), growth-based DST to follow.

cues.text: Growth-based testing asks whether the isolate can grow at a drug’s critical concentration. In the agar proportion method, quadrants of Middlebrook agar contain each drug, and a drug-free quadrant gets the same inoculum diluted one in one hundred.

The rule: if colonies on a drug quadrant are more than one percent of the colonies on the drug-free control, the isolate is resistant to that drug. The diluted control is a built-in one-percent yardstick.
Growth takes time. One review lists about three to four weeks for agar testing, and twenty-eight to forty-two days or longer once the isolate itself must first be grown.

So molecular and growth-based tests work together. The 2017 American guideline recommends rapid molecular rifampicin testing for smear-positive patients at risk of resistance, such as prior treatment, HIV, or contact with multidrug-resistant tuberculosis.

props.title: Fast first, growth to follow
lines: At-risk patient: rapid molecular Rif test
Growth-based DST for the full drug panel

scenes.title: RIPE, the four-drug panel and M. bovis
scenes.altText: Cards: “RIPE (ATS/CDC/IDSA 2016)” — intensive phase 2 months isoniazid, rifampin, pyrazinamide, ethambutol; continuation 4 months isoniazid and rifampin. “Baseline DST” — isoniazid, rifampin, ethambutol and pyrazinamide; ethambutol can stop once the isolate is susceptible to isoniazid and rifampin. “M. bovis” — MTB complex member; intrinsic pyrazinamide resistance from a natural pncA mutation or deletion (pncA encodes pyrazinamidase, which converts PZA to pyrazinoic acid); spread via infected cattle or unpasteurised dairy; Xpert cannot differentiate it. Hook answers card.

cues.text: The American guideline’s preferred regimen for adults with drug-susceptible tuberculosis is RIPE: two months of rifampin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide and ethambutol, then four months of isoniazid and rifampin.
So baseline susceptibility testing covers all four drugs. Ethambutol can be stopped once the isolate is shown to be susceptible to isoniazid and rifampin.

Mycobacterium bovis belongs to the tuberculosis complex and is intrinsically resistant to pyrazinamide: a natural pncA change disables pyrazinamidase, the enzyme that turns the drug into its active acid. It spreads from cattle and unpasteurised dairy.

Back to the hook. One: treat rifampicin resistance as likely, and confirm with growth-based testing. Two: three percent is more than one percent, so resistant to isoniazid. Three: suspect bovis and identify the species.

props.title: Baseline DST: all four
lines: Stop EMB if INH + RIF susceptible

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards: “M. bovis is pyrazinamide-susceptible like M. tuberculosis” (✓ intrinsically resistant, pncA); “A negative Xpert on smear-negative sputum rules out TB” (✓ pooled sensitivity only 67% in smear-negative culture-positive disease; a negative NAAT cannot exclude pulmonary TB); “3% growth on drug means 97% killed, so susceptible” (✓ more than 1% of control = resistant).

cues.text: Trap one: Mycobacterium bovis is pyrazinamide-susceptible like tuberculosis. No: it is intrinsically resistant, through pncA.
Trap two: a negative cartridge test on smear-negative sputum rules out tuberculosis. No: sensitivity is only about two-thirds there, and culture is still needed.
Trap three: three percent growth means most bacilli were killed, so call it susceptible. No: more than one percent of the control is resistant.

scenes.title: RIPE fruit, one bad apple, cows skip the P
scenes.altText: Memory aid: “Treatment is RIPE fruit. One bad apple in a hundred spoils the barrel: more than 1% growth on drug = resistant. Cows skip the P: M. bovis ignores pyrazinamide.” Tokens: RIPE = 4 drugs · 1 in 100 = resistant · cows skip P = bovis. A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: treatment is RIPE fruit, four drugs. One bad apple in a hundred spoils the barrel: more than one percent growth on drug means resistant. And cows skip the P: bovis ignores pyrazinamide.

Where it breaks: the one-percent rule is taught here only for the agar proportion method at critical concentrations, so do not assume it for other methods; RIPE is the American first-line regimen and other programmes may differ; and bovis is not the only pyrazinamide-resistant complex member, since tuberculosis can acquire it.

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “Xpert = MTB complex + rifampicin resistance in under 2 hours; negative ≠ no TB if smear-negative”, “Growth-based DST: drug colonies more than 1% of control = resistant · RIPE panel · PZA-resistant only → think bovis”.

cues.text: Xpert MTB/RIF gives a two-hour answer on tuberculosis complex and rifampicin resistance, but growth-based testing still matters, where more than one percent growth on drug means resistant and a pyrazinamide-only resistant isolate suggests Mycobacterium bovis.

props.label: Xpert: MTBC + Rif-R in < 2 h · smear − and negative ≠ no TB
> 1% of control = R · test all of RIPE · PZA-R only → bovis

explanation.what: Plain language: one fast cartridge test finds tuberculosis DNA and checks the gene where rifampicin resistance usually arises; slower growth-based tests then check every drug by seeing whether the bacteria can still grow on it. Scientific terms: Xpert MTB/RIF (cartridge real-time PCR), rpoB, rifampicin-resistance-determining region, molecular beacons, Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex (MTBC), phenotypic drug susceptibility testing (DST), agar proportion method, critical concentration, proportional control, RIPE (rifampin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide, ethambutol), pncA, pyrazinamidase, pyrazinoic acid.
explanation.why: Most rifampicin resistance comes from mutations in a short rpoB region, so a probe check of that region gives a same-day warning. Growth-based testing is still needed because it covers the full drug panel. M. bovis carries a natural pncA change, so pyrazinamidase cannot activate pyrazinamide.
explanation.measure: Xpert MTB/RIF (Cochrane 2019 pooled): TB sensitivity 98% smear-positive, 67% smear-negative culture-positive, specificity 98%; rifampicin resistance sensitivity 96%, specificity 98%; result within 2 hours. Agar proportion: drug quadrants at critical concentrations, drug-free proportional control inoculated with a 1:100 dilution; resistant when drug-quadrant colonies are more than 1% of control colonies. Treatment (ATS/CDC/IDSA 2016): 2 months INH + RIF + PZA + EMB, then 4 months INH + RIF; baseline DST for INH, RIF, EMB and PZA.
explanation.differs: Molecular (rpoB mutations; rifampicin only; hours) vs growth-based (all drugs; weeks). M. tuberculosis (pyrazinamide susceptible unless resistance is acquired) vs M. bovis (intrinsically pyrazinamide resistant). Xpert detects the complex and cannot separate the two.
explanation.examAngle: Expect: read a proportion result (for example 3% growth on isoniazid = resistant), name the gene behind Xpert’s rifampicin call, recognise that a negative Xpert in smear-negative sputum does not exclude TB, or identify M. bovis from a pyrazinamide-only resistant MTBC isolate.

mnemonic.text: Treatment is RIPE fruit (four drugs). One bad apple in a hundred spoils the barrel: more than 1% growth on drug = resistant. Cows skip the P: M. bovis ignores pyrazinamide.
mnemonic.explanation: Links the four-drug panel, the proportion threshold and the bovine species with intrinsic pyrazinamide resistance.
mnemonic.limitation: The 1% rule is taught here only for the agar proportion method at critical concentrations and should not be assumed for other DST methods; RIPE is the US first-line regimen and other programmes may differ; M. bovis is not the only pyrazinamide-resistant complex member, because M. tuberculosis can acquire resistance.

analogyLimitations: The rpoB and plate drawings are schematic.
Accuracy figures are pooled review estimates; individual studies and settings differ.
takeaway: Xpert MTB/RIF gives a two-hour answer on tuberculosis complex and rifampicin resistance, but growth-based testing still matters, where more than one percent growth on drug means resistant and a pyrazinamide-only resistant isolate suggests Mycobacterium bovis.

questions.stem: In the agar proportion method, colonies on the isoniazid quadrant equal 3% of the colonies on the drug-free control quadrant. How is the isolate reported for isoniazid?

options.rationale: Correct. Growth on the drug quadrant of more than 1% of the control count defines resistance.

options.text: Susceptible, because 97% of the population was inhibited
options.rationale: Incorrect. The threshold is 1%, not a majority; 3% exceeds it.
Incorrect. The 1% rule classifies the isolate as resistant or susceptible at the critical concentration; 3% is above the threshold, so resistant.

options.text: Uninterpretable until Xpert MTB/RIF is run
options.rationale: Incorrect. Xpert MTB/RIF detects rifampicin-resistance mutations in rpoB; it does not test isoniazid.

questions.stem: A patient with suspected pulmonary tuberculosis has a smear-negative sputum that is negative by Xpert MTB/RIF. What is the best interpretation?

options.text: Tuberculosis is not excluded; culture is still needed
options.rationale: Correct. Pooled sensitivity in smear-negative, culture-positive disease is about 67%, and a negative NAAT cannot exclude pulmonary TB.
Incorrect. About a third of smear-negative, culture-positive cases are missed.
Incorrect. Xpert reports rifampicin resistance alongside a positive MTB complex result; when no MTB complex is detected, the test gives no susceptibility information.

options.text: The patient has M. bovis, which Xpert cannot detect
options.rationale: Incorrect. Xpert detects the MTB complex, which includes M. bovis; it simply cannot tell the species apart.

questions.stem: An MTB complex isolate is resistant to pyrazinamide but susceptible to isoniazid, rifampin and ethambutol. The patient regularly drinks unpasteurised milk. Which organism is most likely?

options.rationale: Correct. M. bovis is intrinsically pyrazinamide resistant through a natural pncA change and spreads through unpasteurised dairy.
Incorrect. Multidrug resistance means resistance to at least isoniazid and rifampin, which this isolate lacks.

options.text: Mycobacterium tuberculosis that acquired pyrazinamide resistance
options.rationale: Incorrect as the most likely answer. M. tuberculosis can acquire pncA mutations, but pyrazinamide-only resistance plus unpasteurised-dairy exposure points first to M. bovis, which is intrinsically resistant; species identification decides.
Incorrect. The isolate is rifampin susceptible.

references.citation: Yusoof KA, García JI, Schami A, et al. Tuberculosis Phenotypic and Genotypic Drug Susceptibility Testing and Immunodiagnostics: A Review. Front Immunol. 2022;13:870768. doi:10.3389/fimmu.2022.870768
references.usedFor: MDR-TB defined as resistance to at least isoniazid and rifampicin; proportion method on 7H10/7H11 agar; resistance defined by about 1% growth on drug compared with drug-free growth; agar DST 21–28 days (Table 1) and 28–42 days or longer when the isolate must first be grown; rifampicin resistance (rpoB) as MDR surrogate; Xpert followed by phenotypic DST in some cases.

Comparison between the BACTEC MGIT 960 system and the agar proportion method for susceptibility testing of multidrug resistant tuberculosis strains in a high burden setting of South Africa. BMC Infect Dis. 2012;12:369. doi:10.1186/1471-2334-12-369
references.usedFor: CLSI-based agar proportion protocol: six-well 7H11 plates, drug wells at critical concentrations, drug-free proportional control inoculated with a 1:100 dilution; read at 7, 10, 14 and 21 days; resistant when drug-quadrant colonies are more than 1% of control colonies.

references.citation: Fang Y, Wang F, Ji J, et al. Disseminated Pyrazinamide-Resistant Mycobacterium Bovis in an AIDS Patient: The Role of Molecular Diagnosis and Optimized Therapy. Infect Drug Resist. 2025;18:2599-2604. doi:10.2147/IDR.S522721
references.usedFor: M. bovis is an MTBC member spread via infected cattle or unpasteurised dairy; intrinsic pyrazinamide resistance from a natural pncA mutation or deletion (pncA encodes pyrazinamidase, which converts PZA to pyrazinoic acid); PZA resistance in M. tuberculosis is usually acquired; GeneXpert cannot differentiate M. bovis.

references.citation: Singh AV, Yadav VS, Chauhan DS, Singh SV. Mycobacterium bovis induced human tuberculosis in India: Current status, challenges & opportunities. Indian J Med Res. 2022;156(1):21-30. doi:10.4103/ijmr.ijmr_1161_19
references.usedFor: M. bovis intrinsically resistant to pyrazinamide; routine tests and CBNAAT/GeneXpert do not differentiate M. bovis from M. tuberculosis; checking pyrazinamide resistance in suspected zoonotic TB; humans infected through close contact with infected animals or contaminated milk; TB patients can transmit M. tuberculosis to in-contact people by the aerosol route.

claims.text: Xpert MTB/RIF amplifies an MTB-specific rpoB sequence and uses molecular beacons on the region where most rifampicin-resistance mutations lie; MTBC plus rifampicin resistance within 2 hours.
Pooled accuracy: 98% smear-positive, 67% smear-negative, specificity 98%; rifampicin resistance 96%/98%.
claims.note: Differs from the reviewer’s 100% specificity and 69–72% smear-negative figures; register flag rv-xpert-pooled-accuracy.

claims.text: A negative NAAT cannot exclude pulmonary TB in a smear-negative patient; rapid molecular rifampin testing for at-risk patients.
Xpert detects the MTB complex and cannot differentiate M. bovis from M. tuberculosis.
Agar proportion method: critical concentrations, 1:100 diluted drug-free control, resistant when drug colonies exceed 1% of control; agar DST weeks.
claims.note: Said 2012 states “more than 1%”; Yusoof 2022 states “at least 1%”. The lesson uses “more than 1%”, matching the CLSI-based protocol. The “built-in 1% yardstick” wording is arithmetic from the 1:100 dilution.

claims.text: RIPE intensive phase and continuation phase; baseline DST for INH, RIF, EMB and PZA; stop EMB once INH and RIF susceptible.

M. bovis: MTBC member, intrinsic pyrazinamide resistance via pncA/pyrazinamidase; spread mainly zoonotically from cattle and unpasteurised dairy; M. tuberculosis usually acquires PZA resistance and spreads between people by aerosol.
Xpert targets an 81-bp rpoB fragment with hands-on time under 5 minutes; 28-day susceptibility turnaround target; M. bovis niacin- and nitrate-negative.
claims.note: Not taught. Boehme 2010 uses the 81-bp core region for confirmatory sequencing and reports hands-on time under 15 minutes.

claims.text: Scenario invented; gene and plate drawings schematic.
“RIPE fruit, one bad apple, cows skip the P.”

accuracyFlags.issue: Ch. 59 Hit 6 and the Number Vault give Xpert MTB/RIF smear-negative sensitivity as 69–72%, and the Number Vault gives specificity as 100%. The 2019 Cochrane review gives pooled specificity of 98% (unselected participants) and smear-negative, culture-positive sensitivity of 67% (62–72%); the lesson teaches the pooled figures (register flag rv-xpert-pooled-accuracy).

The RIPE regimen, the four-drug baseline DST panel and the rapid rifampin-testing criteria taught here come from US ATS/CDC/IDSA guidelines. Philippine National TB Program rules are not covered; MTLE candidates should check local requirements.

morphology.note: No micrographs or plate photographs; the gene and agar plate are schematic cards.
